root_cause.text: In procfs `do_procmap_query()`, error handling for the build-ID size check reused the `out` cleanup path after `mmput(mm)` had already been performed, causing a second `mmput()` on the same `mm_struct`.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states the `-ENAMETOOLONG` condition “happens later, after we unlocked mmap_lock/per-VMA lock and did mmput(), so original goto out is now wrong and will double-mmput() mm_struct,” and the patch changes `goto out;` to `goto out_file;`, skipping the `out:` block that calls `query_vma_teardown(&lock_ctx); mmput(mm);`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the short build-ID buffer error path in `do_procmap_query()` to use the file cleanup exit path and avoid missing resource cleanup.
intent_record.what: The error path taken when `karg.build_id_size < build_id_sz` in `do_procmap_query()` was changed from `goto out;` to `goto out_file;` while leaving the `err = -ENAMETOOLONG;` assignment unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this redirects the insufficient-build-id-buffer error through the `out_file` cleanup path instead of the more general `out` path, ensuring any file-related state acquired earlier in the function is properly released before returning the error.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a dedicated cleanup label so error paths can jump directly to vm_file release and shared teardown logic.
intent_record.what: A new label named "out_file:" was inserted immediately before the existing cleanup block that conditionally calls fput(vm_file) and then kfree(name_buf).
intent_record.how: This creates an additional jump target for error or exit paths so execution can branch directly to the file-release cleanup section, ensuring vm_file is dropped and subsequent cleanup runs in the correct order.

consistency_review.core_intent: Refactor do_procmap_query() error handling to route failures through a dedicated vm_file cleanup path so resources are consistently released.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly modify do_procmap_query() error handling and introduce a dedicated cleanup path for the short build-ID buffer case, which matches the root cause of using the wrong cleanup label after mmput(mm) and causing a double mmput().

candidates.rationale: On the short build-ID buffer error path, this jump reuses the generic out cleanup label after mmput(mm) had already been performed earlier in the function, leading to a second mmput() on the same mm_struct.
This cleanup statement at the out label is executed when the erroneous goto out path is taken, causing the double mmput because mm had already been released before reaching this label.

vuln_statements.explanation: This jump is the root cause: on the short build-ID buffer error path in do_procmap_query(), control transfers to the generic out cleanup label even though mmput(mm) has already been called earlier, resulting in the same mm_struct being released again.
This cleanup at the out label becomes vulnerable in combination with the erroneous goto out path, because it performs a second mmput() on an mm_struct that was already released before the jump.
